In all of these appearances Nash wore his typical black tuxedo, top hat, and dark sunglasses, but not his signature bandages. He was also photographed in this attire for a profile in the *[Toronto Star](/wiki/Toronto_Star "Toronto Star")*, published April 28, 1978.[[7]](#cite_note-Star1978-7)

In later years, he attempted to keep his true identity the subject of some speculation, although the *Star* profile of 1978 had already matter-of-factly revealed his real name.[[7]](#cite_note-Star1978-7) Nevertheless, in a 1981 interview with the UK magazine *[Smash Hits](/wiki/Smash_Hits "Smash Hits")*, Nash was questioned about his real name, and replied with "Nashville Thebodiah Slasher". As a result of his coyness about his name, some fans came to believe that the Nash persona was an alter-ego of [Ben Mink](/wiki/Ben_Mink "Ben Mink"), who replaced him as FM's violinist and mandolinist in 1978. This is a common misconception, but he has been photographed onstage with Mink.[[8]](#cite_note-photo1-8)

The rivalry between the [Dallas Cowboys](/wiki/Dallas_Cowboys "Dallas Cowboys") and the 49ers has lasted since the 1970s. The [NFL Top 10](/wiki/NFL_Top_10 "NFL Top 10") ranked this rivalry to be the tenth best in NFL history. San Francisco has played Dallas in nine postseason games. The Cowboys defeated the 49ers in the 1970 and 1971 NFC Championship Games, and again in the 1972 Divisional Playoff Game. The 1981 NFC Championship Game in San Francisco, which saw the 49ers' [Joe Montana](/wiki/Joe_Montana "Joe Montana") complete a game-winning pass to [Dwight Clark](/wiki/Dwight_Clark "Dwight Clark") in the final minute (now known as **The Catch**), is one of the most famous games in NFL history. The rivalry became even more intense during the 1992–1994 seasons. San Francisco and Dallas faced each other in the NFC Championship Game three separate times. Dallas won the first two match-ups, and San Francisco won the third. In each of these pivotal match-ups, the game's victor went on to win the Super Bowl. Both the Cowboys and the 49ers are third all-time in [Super Bowl](/wiki/Super_Bowl "Super Bowl") victories to the [Pittsburgh Steelers](/wiki/Pittsburgh_Steelers "Pittsburgh Steelers") and [New England Patriots](/wiki/New_England_Patriots "New England Patriots") with five each. The 49ers–Cowboys rivalry is also part of the larger cultural rivalry between California and Texas. In recent years, this once-great rivalry has greatly softened, with the struggles of both the Cowboys and 49ers. However, in its prime especially in the 1990s, this rivalry was a very bitter one as both teams were the class of the NFL during this time. In what was believed to be the greatest upset in the team's rivalry in the modern era, the 49ers upset the Cowboys in the 2021 Wild Card Round.

After the 1949 season, the JBL team owners reorganized into the NPB; [Daiei Stars](/wiki/Daiei_Stars "Daiei Stars") owner [Masaichi Nagata](/wiki/Masaichi_Nagata "Masaichi Nagata") promoted a two-league system, which became the [Pacific League](/wiki/Pacific_League "Pacific League") (initially called the Taiheiyo Baseball Union) and the [Central League](/wiki/Central_League "Central League"), with Nagata becoming the first president of the Pacific League.[[12]](#cite_note-Fame-12) The league now known as Nippon Professional Baseball began play in 1950.

Four JBL teams formed the basis of the Central League: the [Chunichi Dragons](/wiki/Chunichi_Dragons "Chunichi Dragons"), the [Hanshin Tigers](/wiki/Hanshin_Tigers "Hanshin Tigers"), the [Yomiuri Giants](/wiki/Yomiuri_Giants "Yomiuri Giants"), and the [Shochiku Robins](/wiki/Shochiku_Robins "Shochiku Robins") (formerly the Taiyō Robins). To fill out the league, four new teams were formed: the [Hiroshima Carp](/wiki/Hiroshima_Carp "Hiroshima Carp"), the [Kokutetsu Swallows](/wiki/Kokutetsu_Swallows "Kokutetsu Swallows"), the [Nishi Nippon Pirates](/wiki/Nishi_Nippon_Pirates "Nishi Nippon Pirates"), and the [Taiyō Whales](/wiki/Taiy%C5%8D_Whales "Taiyō Whales").

Four JBL teams formed the basis of the Pacific League: the [Hankyu Braves](/wiki/Hankyu_Braves "Hankyu Braves"), the [Nankai Hawks](/wiki/Nankai_Hawks "Nankai Hawks"), the [Daiei Stars](/wiki/Daiei_Stars "Daiei Stars"), and the [Tokyu Flyers](/wiki/Tokyu_Flyers "Tokyu Flyers"). To fill out the league, three new teams were formed: the [Kintetsu Pearls](/wiki/Kintetsu_Pearls "Kintetsu Pearls"), the [Mainichi Orions](/wiki/Mainichi_Orions "Mainichi Orions"), and the [Nishitetsu Clippers](/wiki/Nishitetsu_Clippers "Nishitetsu Clippers").

[Matsutarō Shōriki](/wiki/Matsutar%C5%8D_Sh%C5%8Driki "Matsutarō Shōriki"), the Giants' owner, acted as NPB's unofficial commissioner and oversaw the first [Japan Series](/wiki/Japan_Series "Japan Series"), which featured the Mainichi Orions defeating the Shochiku Robins 4 games to 2.

At certain points on Mercury's surface, an observer would be able to see the Sun peek up a little more than two-thirds of the way over the horizon, then reverse and set before rising again, all within the same [Mercurian day](/wiki/Extraterrestrial_skies#Mercury "Extraterrestrial skies").[[a]](#cite_note-angular-117) This is because approximately four Earth days before perihelion, Mercury's angular [orbital velocity](/wiki/Orbital_speed "Orbital speed") equals its angular [rotational velocity](/wiki/Rotational_velocity "Rotational velocity") so that the Sun's [apparent motion](/wiki/Improper_motion "Improper motion") ceases; closer to perihelion, Mercury's angular orbital velocity then exceeds the angular rotational velocity. Thus, to a hypothetical observer on Mercury, the Sun appears to move in a [retrograde](/wiki/Apparent_retrograde_motion "Apparent retrograde motion") direction. Four Earth days after perihelion, the Sun's normal apparent motion resumes.[[28]](#cite_note-strom-28) A similar effect would have occurred if Mercury had been in synchronous rotation: the alternating gain and loss of rotation over a revolution would have caused a libration of 23.65° in longitude.[[117]](#cite_note-118)

For the same reason, there are two points on Mercury's equator, 180 degrees apart in [longitude](/wiki/Longitude "Longitude"), at either of which, around perihelion in alternate Mercurian years (once a Mercurian day), the Sun passes overhead, then reverses its apparent motion and passes overhead again, then reverses a second time and passes overhead a third time, taking a total of about 16 Earth-days for this entire process. In the other alternate Mercurian years, the same thing happens at the other of these two points. The amplitude of the retrograde motion is small, so the overall effect is that, for two or three weeks, the Sun is almost stationary overhead, and is at its most brilliant because Mercury is at perihelion, its closest to the Sun. A **die** (plural: **dice**, sometimes also used as singular)[[1]](#cite_note-1) is a small, throwable object with marked sides that can rest in multiple positions. Dice are used for generating [random values](/wiki/Statistical_randomness "Statistical randomness"), commonly as part of [tabletop games](/wiki/Tabletop_game "Tabletop game"), including [dice games](/wiki/List_of_dice_games "List of dice games"), [board games](/wiki/Board_game "Board game"), [role-playing games](/wiki/Role-playing_game "Role-playing game"), and [games of chance](/wiki/Game_of_chance "Game of chance").

A traditional die is a [cube](/wiki/Cube "Cube") with each of its six faces marked with a different number of dots ([pips](/wiki/Pip_(counting) "Pip (counting)")) from 1 to 6. When thrown or rolled, the die comes to rest showing a random [integer](/wiki/Integer "Integer") from one to six on its upper surface, with each value being equally likely. Dice may also have other [polyhedral](/wiki/Polyhedron "Polyhedron") or irregular shapes, may have faces marked with numerals or symbols instead of pips and may have their numbers carved out from the material of the dice instead of marked on it. Loaded dice are specifically designed or modified to favor some results over others, for [cheating](/wiki/Cheating "Cheating") or entertainment purposes.

Main article: [Economy of Equatorial Guinea](/wiki/Economy_of_Equatorial_Guinea "Economy of Equatorial Guinea")

Before the nation's independence from Spain, Equatorial Guinea exported [cocoa](/wiki/Cocoa_bean "Cocoa bean"), coffee and timber, mostly to its colonial ruler, Spain, but also to Germany and the UK. On 1 January 1985, the country became the first non-[Francophone](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/Francophone "wikt:Francophone") African member of the [franc zone](/wiki/Franc_zone "Franc zone"), adopting the [CFA franc](/wiki/CFA_franc "CFA franc") as its currency. The national currency, the [ekwele](/wiki/Ekwele "Ekwele"), had previously been linked to the [Spanish peseta](/wiki/Spanish_peseta "Spanish peseta").[[111]](#cite_note-web.archive.org-113)
